beats.narration: DeepSeek V3 point two lets each token look at just two thousand forty-eight earlier tokens. Who picks them, and what stays quadratic?

props.title: DeepSeek-V3.2, Sparse Enough?
thesis: Same 671B / 37B base as V3, continued from V3.1-Terminus. One change:
a cheap indexer decides where each token looks before attention runs.

roadmap.label: The indexer
roadmap.body: 64 small FP8 heads score every earlier token.

roadmap.label: Still quadratic
roadmap.body: The indexer itself still touches every pair.

beats.narration: Each layer now attends in two passes. A lightning indexer, sixty-four small heads, scores every earlier token. Only the top two thousand forty-eight reach the real attention.
beats.narration_text: Each layer now attends in two passes. A lightning indexer, sixty-four small heads, scores every earlier token. Only the top two thousand forty-eight reach the real attention.

props.spark: A cheap pass, then an expensive one.
props.heading: DeepSeek Sparse Attention, per layer

moves.label: INDEX
moves.detail: 64 heads × 128 dims, in FP8, score every earlier token.

moves.label: SELECT
moves.detail: Keep the 2,048 highest-scoring tokens for each query.

moves.label: ATTEND
moves.detail: Multi-head latent attention runs over only those 2,048.

moves.label: UNCHANGED
moves.detail: Everything else is V3: 256 + 1 experts, 61 layers.

props.keepNote: Row 1 is the new part. Main attention only ever sees what the indexer keeps.
props.source: config.json: index_n_heads 64 · index_head_dim 128 · index_topk 2048 · DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp report

beats.narration: Count at a hundred thirty-one thousand tokens. Dense attention scores about eight point six billion query key pairs. Sparse main attention, two hundred sixty-eight million: thirty-two times fewer. But the indexer still scores all eight point six billion.
beats.narration_text: Count at a hundred thirty-one thousand tokens. Dense attention scores about eight point six billion query key pairs. Sparse main attention, two hundred sixty-eight million: thirty-two times fewer. But the indexer still scores all eight point six billion.

props.heading: Query–key pairs at 131,072 tokens
props.exception: Main attention: 32x fewer pairs. The indexer still scores all ≈ 8.6B — cheaper per pair, not fewer pairs.

beats.narration: So what's still quadratic? The indexer: cheaper per pair, not fewer pairs. And selection is a hard cut. A token it misses, main attention never sees. DeepSeek reports quality on par with its last model.
beats.narration_text: So what's still quadratic? The indexer: cheaper per pair, not fewer pairs. And selection is a hard cut. A token it misses, main attention never sees. DeepSeek reports quality on par with its last model.

props.spark: Cheaper per pair, not fewer pairs.
props.heading: What's still quadratic

moves.label: INDEXER
moves.detail: Scores every earlier token: lighter heads and FP8, but still O(L²).

moves.label: HARD CUT
moves.detail: A token the indexer misses is invisible to main attention.

moves.label: QUALITY
moves.detail: On par with V3.1-Terminus, per DeepSeek; the release is labelled experimental.

props.keepNote: Sparse main attention, dense index. Row 2 is the risk worth testing.

beats.narration: Sparse enough? For the expensive part, yes. But the indexer keeps a quadratic core, and a missed token is simply gone.
beats.narration_text: Sparse enough? For the expensive part, yes. But the indexer keeps a quadratic core, and a missed token is simply gone.

artifactLines: Mechanism: a 64-head FP8 indexer picks 2,048 tokens per query; MLA attends only to those.
Count: 32x fewer main-attention pairs at 131K tokens.
Still quadratic: the indexer — cheaper per pair, not fewer pairs.
Risk: a missed token is invisible to main attention.

beats.narration: Your turn. Hide two facts far apart in long documents, then three. If the sparse model falls behind its dense sibling, the indexer is dropping them.
beats.narration_text: Build 20 long documents (~100K tokens) where the answer depends on two facts placed far apart. Ask a sparse-attention model and a dense model of the same family. Report accuracy for both. Then repeat with three facts. Does sparse selection drop the second or third fact?
